currentContext.strengths: Leadership in stainless steel tubes & pipes (#1 in India) and strong/#1 presence in carbon steel welded pipes|Wide product portfolio serving critical, specialised industrial applications across multiple metallurgical grades|Multi-location manufacturing infrastructure in Gujarat and Odisha designed to scale with expansion|Strong global approvals from end users, EPC contractors, and licensors that require years of rigorous auditing, acting as a formidable barrier to entry and allowing a pivot from commodity pricing to engineering-complexity-based pricing|Capability to engineer high-specification products for hydrogen, nuclear, and advanced process applications; first Indian supplier of hydrogen-compliant carbon steel welded pipes|Strong balance sheet, healthy cash flows, and disciplined capital allocation; virtually net-cash entity with negative net debt-to-equity|Strategic diversification through subsidiaries, joint ventures and an international presence (USA, UAE, Europe, Saudi Arabia)|Working-capital buffer of approximately 200 days of inventory coverage, insulating operations from supply-chain disruption and specialty-steel price spikes
currentContext.strategies: Pivoted by design from a volume-driven manufacturer to a specialised, value-accretive engineering partner, focusing on fortifying margins, building durable moats and staying relevant across cycles.|Product-mix optimisation and value enhancement, with a calibrated shift towards higher-margin, specialised product categories.|Continued expansion of global market presence to capitalise on emerging energy and infrastructure capex cycles, kept elevating global vendor approvals to unlock access to specialised, niche end-use industries.|Geographic diversification and localisation: Saudi Arabia JV manufacturing facility for stainless steel tubes, full ownership of Ratnamani Trade EU AG for European distribution, wholly-owned marketing entities in the US and UAE to bypass local content barriers and sharpen export execution.|Subsidiary ecosystem deliberately built to diversify earnings and capture high-margin opportunities in nuclear piping/spooling and precision engineering (bearing rings).|Carbon Steel segment strategy centred on physical capacity expansion (CSAW, HSAW) to widen the 'economic moat' and remain partner of choice for the most technically demanding energy and water infrastructure projects worldwide.|Balanced dual-engine portfolio approach combining high-margin specialised SSTP products with high-volume, infrastructure-linked carbon steel pipes to capture both cyclical infrastructure demand and structural shifts towards specialised materials.|Adaptability strategy: agile supply chain and diversified geographic footprint to respond quickly to shifting demand across domestic infrastructure, Middle Eastern energy and European hydrogen projects, avoiding dependence on any single market or sector.
currentContext.expansion: Ratnamani's manufacturing platform is expanding across integrated facilities in Gujarat and Odisha, each purpose-built for stainless steel seamless tubes, welded tubes, carbon steel pipes, coating systems and specialised downstream processing, backed by group businesses in precision forging (Ravi Technoforge) and specialised spool fabrication (RFSS). At the Odisha plant, Phase I of the helically submerged arc welded (HSAW) pipe line has already been commissioned, adding production flexibility for large-diameter carbon steel applications; Phase II, a coating plant to support this line, is due for completion by July 2026. At Kutch, the plant received API monogram certification from the American Petroleum Institute during the year, opening qualification-led opportunities in stainless steel line pipes under API 5LC standards; the brownfield CSAW expansion was completed, scaling capacity from 48,000 MT to 75,000 MT a year and engineered for high-thickness pipes up to 150 mm thick, 18 metres long and up to 60 MT per pipe. In parallel, expansion is underway for high-thickness C-SAW and H-SAW pipes, with completion targeted for June 2026; a new 1,00,000 MT HSAW spiral pipe facility is under construction at Kutch to produce pipes up to 120 inches in diameter in 18-metre lengths, and combined HSAW capacity is referenced elsewhere in the AR at up to 1,50,000 MT with thickness up to 25.4 mm and diameter up to 200 inches. Ravi Technoforge is expanding into the large-volume bearing rings segment with new automotive component capabilities through a high-speed hot-forming facility, with a commissioning target of March 2027. Ratnamani Middle East Company LLC (the Saudi JV, with Tamimi Group) obtained commercial registration and began setting up its cold-finished stainless steel seamless products manufacturing facility in Dammam from January 2026, with trial production targeted for Q1 FY2027-28. Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions (RFSS) is scaling up via an 80,000 sq. metre fabrication facility (a new 52,000 sq. metre greenfield facility in Kutch is cited elsewhere) and new equipment including Heavy Induction Bending Machines, expanding fabrication capacity from 1,500 MT to 4,000 MT for pipes up to 18 metres in length, prioritising nuclear-sector spooling for domestic and export markets. Export revenue reached ₹1,362.48 Crores in FY2025-26. Other capability additions during the year (2020-2026 timeline) included: the first order for Sour Service (transporting sour crude); enhanced tube pilgering capacity up to 4 inches in diameter; a commissioned modern Tube Coiler Plant; an advanced vacuum surface and ID cleaning system for stainless steel tubes in coil form; a commissioned 1 MW rooftop solar power plant at Indrad; Industry 4.0 and IT-OT integration across the manufacturing unit; NSF approval for SS pipe supplies to the US drinking-water market; and an API 5LC monogramming license for stainless steel welded line pipes. Energy-conservation capital investment during the year included ₹7.21 Lakhs for LED lighting fixtures at Indrad & Kutch plants, ₹73.00 Lakhs for VFD for the conveyor at Kutch plant, and ₹11.00 Lakhs for a 25 KW rooftop solar system at the Sundargarh plant.
currentContext.mdna: Global steel demand stabilising at ~1.75 Billion tonnes in CY2025, marking the trough of the cycle, with recovery expected from CY2026 onwards; regional divergence with India, ASEAN and the Middle East leading growth while China and Europe remain structurally weak.|Global steel tubes market (~USD 80-85 Billion) entering a multi-year upcycle driven by a global energy infrastructure investment cycle, particularly ~150 pipeline projects underway in the Middle East, accelerating the shift towards high-value seamless pipes and large-diameter line pipes.|Industry structurally transitioning from commoditised steel towards value-added, application-specific products, supported by energy transition, decarbonisation and industrial policy trends.|China-plus-one supply chain realignment redirecting export inquiries towards Indian manufacturers capable of meeting stringent global certifications.|Energy security and transition dual mandate driving simultaneous demand for standard carbon steel line pipes (oil & gas) and high-specification stainless steel tubes (hydrogen-ready pipelines, LNG terminals); India plans 34,233 km of gas pipeline network expansion and CGD coverage expanding to ~70%+ of population.|Nuclear Fleet Mode implementation (India's mandate to install 10 indigenous 700 MW reactors, tripling nuclear capacity to 22.48 GW by 2031-32) guarantees a multi-year order pipeline for specialised stainless steel seamless tubes and pre-fabricated piping spools.|National Green Hydrogen Mission catalysing investment in hydrogen production and transmission, generating emerging opportunities for hydrogen-ready pipeline systems.|Steel Quality Control Order (QCO) enforcement bans sub-standard imported steel, acting as a protective economic moat for organised, high-quality manufacturers against unorganised players.|Water infrastructure expansion (rapid urbanisation and state-level water distribution schemes, ~₹3.6 Lakh Crores outlay) supports consistent volume demand for carbon steel coated pipes, though domestic EPC execution delays created transient lumpiness in the year.|Middle East executing a generational upgrade of oil, gas and petrochemical infrastructure, driving sustained high-volume demand for corrosion-resistant alloy products and high-grade carbon steel pipes; global pivot to energy security triggering resurgence in nuclear power and LNG infrastructure.|Management expects strong growth across subsidiary operations and a firm rebound in standalone volumes in FY2026-27, driving towards peak utilisation as new manufacturing lines come online.|Company remains optimistic on long-term domestic market growth driven by Government of India infrastructure/industrial initiatives — planned investment by various Ministries in refining capacity, petrochemical complexes, fertiliser manufacturing, city gas distribution, drinking water projects and renewable energy infrastructure (particularly wind) expected to generate substantial demand for steel pipes and tubular products.|Last-quarter dispatches were adversely impacted by geopolitical tensions from the US-Israel-Iran conflict, causing slower customer off-take, shipment delays and a rise in finished goods inventory at year-end.|Active order book exceeding ₹21.60 Billion (Board's Report), supported by a virtually zero-debt balance sheet with massive liquidity reserves and the ₹1,380 Crores capex programme nearing commercialisation.|Exports have accounted for a significant portion of the order book for the last several years, with MENA, the United States and Europe remaining primary consumers of the stainless-steel portfolio.

risks.note: Fluctuations in basic steel, stainless steel inputs and imported alloys directly impact margins; the Company relies on back-to-back procurement aligned with confirmed orders and ~200-day inventory buffers to absorb shocks.
Over 50% of stainless steel raw material requirements are currently imported, exposing the Company to global supply shocks, arbitrary export policies, and fluctuations in import duties.

Import of raw materials and export revenues expose the Company to currency fluctuations; managed via natural hedging from the import-export matrix and forward contracts per Forex Policy, with no speculative trading.

risks.risk: Geopolitical trade risk / ongoing Middle East war
risks.note: Global trade barriers, tariffs and supply-chain rerouting from regional conflicts are a persistent threat; the ongoing war in the Middle East has already raised freight, container and insurance costs and impacted exports, and a prolonged conflict would adversely affect revenues.

risks.risk: Trade protectionism and export market access
risks.note: Increasing protectionism in the EU and US, including quota reductions, 50% tariffs and the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), could adversely impact exports and market access, given exports constitute a significant portion of the order book.

The domestic carbon steel division is highly sensitive to infrastructure project execution velocity; administrative delays in state-level water distribution schemes or deferred environmental clearances for hydrocarbon pipelines cause unpredictable lumpiness in order booking and dispatches.

High dependence on electricity and CNG exposes operations to tariff revisions, demand penalties, supply constraints and volatile fuel costs, particularly for the energy-intensive seamless tube business.

risks.risk: Competition from alternative manufacturing technologies and overcapacity
risks.note: Growing adoption of piercing-route manufacturing and increasing global overcapacity, especially from China and Asia, may intensify price competition and compress margins in commodity-grade segments.

one-line thesis: Strong order inflow in carbon steel (INR 750cr Q2) and nuclear spools (INR 500cr book) is driving momentum, while Saudi cold-finishing plant and RFSS capacity expansion are key value creators; consolidated revenue guidance of INR 7,500cr in 2-3 years hinges on execution of these capex projects.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +23% YoY consolidated (INR 1,191cr); EBITDA/margin: Standalone 16-18% guided; PAT (rptd): Not disclosed; PAT (normalized): Not disclosed; Order book: INR 2,050cr standalone (INR 1,300cr CS, INR 750cr SS); Net debt: Not disclosed
guidance: Revenue growth: Consolidated INR 7,500cr in 2-3 years; Margin: 16-18% standalone, 20-22% blended for RFSS; Order inflow: INR 750cr Q2 carbon steel; Capex/commissioning: Orissa Phase-II (Mar 2026), RFSS capacity (Q1FY27), Saudi plant (Dec 2026), RTL forging line (FY27)
order book & pipeline: Standalone: INR 2,050cr (INR 1,300cr carbon steel, INR 750cr stainless steel); RFSS: INR 500cr (nuclear only); RTL: Not disclosed
segment / subsidiary detail: Carbon Steel: 60% oil & gas, 40% water in line pipes; SS: API 5LC certified, hydrogen-compliant exports to Europe; RFSS: 1,500t capacity now, expanding to 3,000-4,000t by Q1FY27; RTL: 20%+ YoY growth expected, 30-40% export, U.S. exports to Timken; Ravi: INR 360-380cr FY26, INR 450-475cr FY27
growth verticals / optionality: Saudi cold-finishing plant (Dec 2026) enables GCC market access; RFSS expansion into thermal/oil & gas spools (30% of mix); hydrogen-grade seamless tubes; import substitution in forged rings for global OEMs
margins & cost dynamics: Carbon steel margins pressured by water segment demand; SS margins stable; RFSS margins at 33% Q2, targeting 20-22% blended; RTL margins at 13%, potential to 14% by FY27; cost control driving EBITDA in 16-18% range
capex / expansion: Parent: Orissa Phase-II (INR 225cr, Mar 2026), circumferential pipe expansion (Dec 2026); RTL: INR 250cr (automatic forging line, FY27); RFSS: INR 250cr (capacity to 4,000t, Q1FY27); Saudi: INR 250cr (cold finish line, trial Dec 2026)
capital allocation: Capex prioritized for RFSS, Saudi, and RTL expansions; no dividend or buyback mentioned; debt-funded; focus on capacity utilization to achieve INR 7,500cr consolidated revenue
risks & watch-items: U.S. tariffs on stainless steel; Saudi duty risk post-local production (10%); domestic water pipeline tender delays; nuclear spool execution volatility; European quota/tariff changes from Jan 2026
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; highlights order visibility, capacity utilization, and global expansion; avoids margin breakdowns but confirms growth trajectory; acknowledges domestic demand softness but emphasizes export and capex-led growth
non-obvious takeaways: RFSS's INR 500cr order book is entirely nuclear and will be fully executed by Q1FY27 — next order inflection likely in Q3FY26; Saudi plant will export mother hollows from India, preserving higher Indian margins; RTL's U.S. exports are minimal despite Timken supply
